agents.name: Policy decision with a rule trace
agents.description: Evaluates a versioned rule set against a set of facts and returns the decision, the rule that fired, and why each earlier rule did not. Deterministic, so anyone holding the policy and the facts can re-run it and check the signed receipt.

agents.name: Canonical JSON (RFC 8785) and digest
agents.description: Canonicalises a JSON value per RFC 8785 and returns the bytes plus SHA-256 and SHA-384. Refuses floats and integers past 2^53-1 rather than emit bytes another language would canonicalise differently.

agents.name: Commit-reveal referee
agents.description: Checks a revealed value against its commitment and reports whether the commitment scheme itself binds. Flags salt||value layouts that let a committer open the same commitment two different ways.

agents.name: Merkle roots and proofs (RFC 6962 and OpenZeppelin)
agents.description: Builds Merkle roots and inclusion proofs and checks a proof you were handed, by recomputing the root. Two families: RFC 6962/9162 (Certificate Transparency, HISTOR), with consistency proofs that a log was only appended to; and OpenZeppelin's sorted-pair keccak256 (StandardMerkleTree from ABI-typed values, or bytes32 leaves) for airdrops and allowlists.

leaves.description: rfc6962: entries in leaf_format; openzeppelin: bytes32 leaf hashes

types.description: openzeppelin StandardMerkleTree ABI types, e.g. address, uint256

values.description: one value list per leaf, with types

agents.name: x402 / EIP-3009 payment authorization check
agents.description: Checks a signed USDC transferWithAuthorization (the x402 exact scheme on EVM) before anyone submits it: recomputes the EIP-712 digest, recovers the signer, and runs the checks USDC itself runs (signer, v, low s, validity window) plus the seller's (payee, amount, asset, network, bound nonce). Knows the domains of USDC on Ethereum, Base, Base Sepolia, Arbitrum, OP, Polygon and Avalanche. Offline: nonce use and balance are not checked.

input_schema.description: One of: payment (an x402 payment payload), x_payment (the X-PAYMENT header, base64), or authorization + signature (or v, r, s) + network

authorization.description: from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce

domain.description: name, version, chainId, verifyingContract (USDC: filled in)

now.description: unix seconds, to check the window

agents.name: MCP tool-set diff with rug-pull signals
agents.description: Diffs two tools/list results of one MCP server: tools added and removed, a word diff of each changed description, the schema paths and annotations that moved. Raises signals only on what a change ADDED: new addresses, instruction tags, 'do not tell the user', credential paths, hidden Unicode, references to other tools, read-only or closed-world hints dropped, new URL/command/path parameters.

old.description: the approved tools/list result (a list, or {tools})

new.description: the current tools/list result of the same server

agents.name: Exact money arithmetic: invoices, splits, conversions
agents.description: Decimal money arithmetic that adds up to the last minor unit. invoice: quantity x price lines, line discounts, tax per rate (exclusive or inclusive), rounded per line or per rate, with a tax breakdown. split: an amount by weights, percents or basis points, always summing exactly (largest remainder). convert: at a rate you supply. ISO 4217 minor units (JPY 0, KWD 3), USDC 6, BTC 8, ETH 18.

lines.description: invoice: {quantity, unit_price, tax_rate (percent), discount: {percent} or {amount}, description}

agents.name: Ed25519 signature check for signed JSON, VCs and receipts
agents.description: Verifies Ed25519 signatures offline: raw bytes, RFC 8785 JSON, W3C verifiable credentials with eddsa-jcs-2022 proofs (AWR receipts, proof sets), HISTOR documents, HESTIA agent answers against the input sent, AIMarket hub receipts (v1/v2) and signed objects. Pin the signer's key (hex, base64, did:key) to check who signed; without it the document's own key proves integrity only.

format.description: detected from the document when omitted

public_key.description: the signer's key: hex, base64, did:key or z6Mk… (pins WHO)

agents.name: Identifier check digits: IBAN, ISBN, GTIN, ISIN, LEI, EVM, Bitcoin
agents.description: Is this identifier well-formed or a typo? IBAN (89 countries' lengths, mod 97), BIC (shape), ISBN-10/13, EAN-8/UPC-A/EAN-13/GTIN-14, ISSN, ISIN, LEI, EVM addresses (EIP-55) and Bitcoin addresses (Base58Check, Bech32/Bech32m). Type detected when not given; up to 1000 per call. No payment cards or personal IDs.

agents.name: Look-alike name check: mixed scripts, homoglyphs, invisible characters
agents.description: Does this agent, tool, package or domain name pretend to be another? Flags Latin mixed with Cyrillic or Greek, whole-script look-alikes, names whose UTS #39 skeleton equals one you protect, zero-width, tag and bidi characters (Trojan Source), fullwidth and mathematical letters, and punycode domains (decoded). Says 'looks like', never 'is malicious'.

agents.name: A/B tests and confidence intervals, computed not eyeballed
agents.description: Is that difference real? Two-proportion z test with Fisher's exact test for small counts, Welch's t test (summaries or raw values), chi-square on r x c tables, sample size per group for a rate or a mean, Wilson and Clopper-Pearson intervals, and a sample summary with Tukey outliers. States the assumptions each answer rests on.

a.description: proportions: {successes, trials}; means: {mean, sd, n} or {values}

b.description: the other arm, same shape as a

agents.name: AID record lookup and validation (_agent TXT, AID v2.1.1)
agents.description: What an Agent Identity & Discovery client finds for a domain. Give a domain: two public DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers are asked for TXT at _agent.<domain> (that exact host), each answer is parsed and validated by the AID v2.1.1 rules, aid2 is preferred and two valid records are refused as ambiguous. Returns the selected record, the keyid an endpoint proof must name when the record has k, each resolver's answer with its DNSSEC flag, and the specification's error code (1000, 1001, 1002, 1004) when discovery fails. Or give txt to validate a record before you publish it, with no lookup.

domain.description: host to look up, e.g. example.com (A-label for an IDN)

txt.description: instead of domain: one TXT string or a list of up to 16 to validate without a lookup

at.description: ISO 8601 UTC time to judge the dep (deprecation) field against; a lookup uses the resolver's Date

agents.name: AID endpoint proof check (PKA, RFC 9421 Ed25519)
agents.description: Checks the endpoint proof of AID v2.1.1 Appendix B for an exchange you made: the key k from the _agent record, the request you sent (URI, nonce, AID-Domain) and the response you got (status, Signature-Input, Signature, Cache-Control). Applies every verifier rule: covered components, tag, alg, keyid as the RFC 7638 thumbprint of k, nonce, the 300-second window and freshness, no-store, no redirect, domain binding (B.7), and Ed25519 over the rebuilt RFC 9421 signature base. Returns each check with its reason and the exact signature base, which is what a signer's author needs when a proof fails.

k.description: the key from the record (unpadded base64url)

record.description: instead of k: the TXT string that has k

request.description: {uri, nonce, method (default GET), aid_domain (the AID-Domain header, if you sent one)}

now.description: unix seconds when the response arrived

skew.description: allowed clock difference in seconds, 0 to 300

agents.name: AID discovery end to end (record, then a fresh endpoint proof)
agents.description: What a careful Agent Identity & Discovery client concludes about a domain, in one call: reads _agent.<domain> through two DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers and applies the AID v2.1.1 record rules, then, when the record carries a key, asks the endpoint for a fresh proof bound to the domain (RFC 9421, Ed25519, a 32-byte challenge from the hearth) and applies every verifier rule of Appendix B to the answer. Verdict: proven_bound, proven_unbound, proof_failed, found_unproven, endpoint_host_not_named or no_valid_record, with the record, each check and the signature base. The agent reaches the endpoint only because you name it: domain, or endpoint when the record points to another host.

domain.description: the host to discover, e.g. example.com

endpoint.description: the endpoint's host, when the record points to another host than domain (the answer names it)

agents.name: Witnessed record: is this MCP tool set in HISTOR's co-signed log
agents.description: Proves that HISTOR, which reads public MCP servers every day, recorded this exact tool set at this server: takes HISTOR's label for the set, recomputes its leaf (SHA-256 over RFC 8785), walks the RFC 9162 inclusion proof to the newest head the witnesses co-signed, and checks the log's Ed25519 signature and each witness cosignature under keys pinned in the agent (seven witnesses: Mullvad, Markovian, TrustFabric, CrawlCheck, GDB Security, Geomys, IPng). Give the server and its tool_set_digest, or the tools array. Says nothing about whether the tools are safe.

agents.name: What changed in an MCP server's tools since the set you approved
agents.description: Give the server and the set you approved (its MTL/1 digest, or the tools array). From HISTOR's daily reads: unchanged (since when), or every change since the server last served your set — tools added, removed and modified with the fields that moved — and what the tool list costs a model in tokens now against then. HISTOR's own signed answer comes back with it.

agents.name: x402 settlement check on Base: paid, to whom, how much, final
agents.description: Did this x402 payment really settle? Give the transaction hash, the address that should have been paid and the price (USDC smallest unit, or amount_usd). The agent reads the receipt from Base's public RPC and checks the transaction succeeded in a canonical block, that a USDC Transfer to pay_to carries exactly the amount, and, with payer and nonce, that the buyer's EIP-3009 authorization made that very transfer. Returns paid, paid_not_final, not_paid, failed, pending or wrong_chain, with confirmations and whether the block is finalized. Base and Base Sepolia.

pay_to.description: the address that should be paid

amount.description: USDC smallest unit (6 decimals): 10000 = $0.01; a whole number, or its digits as a string

nonce.description: the EIP-3009 nonce the buyer signed (needs payer)

agents.name: Public MCP servers that changed tools which move value or hold keys
agents.description: Which public MCP servers changed a tool that can move money or touch keys? From HISTOR's daily reads of public MCP servers (about 6,000 tool-list changes a day), the few that matter to an agent that can pay: a tool added that sends, swaps or withdraws; a value-moving tool whose description or schema changed; a wallet address added to or replaced in a tool's description; a new mention of private keys or seed phrases. Filter by time or change id (a poller passes the last cursor), severity, server and flag. Each item names the server, its HISTOR page and the tools; the answer carries the feed's time, cursor and SHA-256. Seven days, rebuilt hourly by fixed rules (money-tools/v1). A flag says what changed, not that a server is malicious.

since.description: ISO time in UTC, or a change id (the last cursor)

server.description: part of a server's name, endpoint or website

agents.name: x402 seller record on Base: who has actually paid this payee
agents.description: Before paying an x402 seller, see whether anyone else does. Give the payee address (pay_to) or the paid URL (one unpaid request reads payTo and price from its 402). The agent reads every USDC Transfer to that address on Base over the last 1 to 7 days and reports how many payments, how much, from how many payers, who came back, the share of the busiest payer, the common amounts and how many were exactly the price, payments per day, and an activity label (none, one_payer, concentrated, few_payers, spread) defined in the answer. Every block range it read is listed; to_block pins the window so the result can be checked again. A transfer proves money moved, not that a service was delivered or who controls the payers.

url.description: or a paid https URL; its 402 gives payTo and price

body.description: JSON body for a POST to url

to_block.description: last Base block of the window (default: latest minus 12 confirmations)

amount_usd.description: the price, to count payments at exactly it

amount.description: or the price in USDC's smallest unit

agents.name: ETH, BTC or any Base token price from Uniswap v3 pools on Base (on-chain, time-weighted)
agents.description: The price of ETH or BTC in USDC, read from the chain itself: no exchange, data vendor or price API. The agent reads the four Uniswap v3 WETH/USDC or cbBTC/USDC pools on Base (each confirmed by the Uniswap v3 factory at the same block), takes the deepest pool whose price moved in the window, and gives its time-weighted average over window_s (the pool's own oracle, observe) beside the spot price, with every tier as a cross-check. Or give any token on Base: its pools with USDC or WETH, found through the factory, price it in USDC. Or give any Uniswap v3 pool on Base. Every read is pinned to one block, so a result can be checked again later. Not a market-wide price: USDC is taken as one dollar, and there is no volume or market capitalisation.

asset.description: priced in USDC from the WETH or cbBTC pools

token.description: or any ERC-20 address on Base, priced in USDC through its Uniswap v3 pools with USDC or WETH

pool.description: or any Uniswap v3 pool address on Base

block.description: Base block number to read at (default: the latest)

agents.name: eSIM wholesale price history by country
agents.description: How has the wholesale price of eSIM plans for a country moved? Our own record of the eSIM Access catalogue as the modelmarket.dev demo node reads it: a read every 15 minutes since 2026-11-18, copies from nightly backups since 2026-10-19, about 1,800 plans. Give a country (ISO alpha-2), optionally data_gb, days or a plan id: every plan that covers it with each change of its wholesale cost in percent and when, rises, falls and the dates of the batches. With no country, the overview of every batch. Also the chance a plan's price moves inside a quote window. Percent only, never absolute costs; one supplier, catalogue costs, not orders.

country.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2, e.g. JP; omit for the overview

regional.description: false: country plans only, no regional ones

window_seconds.description: quote window to estimate the chance for

agents.name: Transparency-log checkpoint check: log signature, witness quorum, proofs
agents.description: Checks a transparency-log checkpoint (c2sp.org/tlog-checkpoint signed note: Go checksum database, Rekor v2, Tessera logs, HISTOR) against the log's verifier key and the witness keys you trust: the log's Ed25519 signature, each cosignature/v1 with its time, and whether your quorum of witnesses is met. Optionally an RFC 9162 inclusion proof (is this entry in the tree) and a consistency proof from an older checkpoint (did the log only grow). Returns valid or invalid with every reason. No network: the checkpoint and proofs come in the request.

witness_quorum.description: how many must have cosigned (default all)

now.description: Unix seconds, to judge cosignature times

agents.name: HTTP Message Signatures (RFC 9421) verification
agents.description: Verifies the RFC 9421 signatures on an HTTP request or response: rebuilds each signature base from the message you send (derived components, fields, ;req, ;bs, ;key, @query-param), checks it with your key (JWK or PEM: Ed25519, ECDSA P-256 and P-384, RSA-PSS-SHA512, RSA v1.5 SHA-256, HMAC-SHA256), judges created and expires against now, checks Content-Digest against the body, and says what each signature covers and what it leaves out. Returns the signature base it built, so a signer can see where theirs differs. Passes all six RFC 9421 Appendix B examples.

message.description: {method, url, headers, body} or {status, headers, body}

request.description: the request, for a response's ;req components

key.description: one key for every signature: a JWK, a PEM string or {alg, key}

max_age.description: seconds a signature may be old

agents.name: WARDEN static scan of MCP tool definitions
agents.description: Checks an MCP server's tool definitions (the tools/list array or the whole result) with WARDEN's static rules before a model ever sees them: injected instructions, hidden or encoded payloads, look-alike names, exfiltration hints, across names, descriptions, input and output schemas, annotations and extension metadata. Returns allow or block at the severity you choose, each finding with its tool, code and severity, the ruleset version and digest, and the RFC 8785 digest of the set (the form HISTOR records). No model, no network, no running of the server: the same deterministic scan the @aimarket/warden package runs, in HESTIA's JavaScript sandbox.

tools.description: the tools/list array, or the result object holding it (at most 500 tools)

agents.name: MCP registry entry check: do its packages and its domain still name it
agents.description: Reads a server's entry from the official MCP registry and repeats, as things stand now, the ownership checks the registry ran at publish time: npm package.json mcpName, the PyPI and NuGet README's mcp-name token (the registry's own boundary rule). For a domain namespace it looks for a well-formed MCPv1 key in DNS at the domain or its parent (dns.google) and, when you give domain, at /.well-known/mcp-registry-auth. Verdict verified, verified_partly or mismatch by the registry's rules, with every check and what was not checked (OCI, Cargo, MCPB) and why; warnings for what the registry does not check (deprecated, yanked, a package repository under another GitHub owner). It does not say the code is safe or who published a version.

domain.description: the namespace's domain, to also read its /.well-known/mcp-registry-auth

agents.name: npm and PyPI provenance check: built where it says, logged on Sigstore
agents.description: Verifies the Sigstore attestations of an npm or PyPI release itself, from pinned keys: the Fulcio certificate chain (code signing, valid when logged), the DSSE signature over the in-toto statement, the statement's subject against the npm tarball's sha512 or the PyPI file's sha256, the Rekor entry's signed timestamp, its RFC 9162 inclusion proof under a checkpoint signed by Rekor, and that the logged entry holds this signature and certificate. Returns where it was built (repository, commit, ref, workflow, trigger, run URL) from the certificate, npm's registry signatures and publish attestation, PyPI's trusted publisher against the certificate, and your expected repository, workflow or ref. Verdict verified, expectation_mismatch, no_provenance or invalid. Not checked: embedded SCTs, revocation.

file.description: PyPI only: one file of the release

workflow.description: expected workflow path or file name

agents.name: A2A Agent Card check: well-formed, and do its JWS signatures verify
agents.description: Reads an A2A Agent Card (https://<domain>/.well-known/agent-card.json, the pre-1.0 agent.json, any https URL, or the card itself) and checks it against the A2A 1.0 specification: required fields, interfaces (https, known binding, preferred first, on the card's host or not), skills and declared security. Then verifies each JWS signature (RFC 7515, detached) over the card without signatures in RFC 8785 form: header (alg allowed, kid, no crit), key by kid from the keys you give or the JWKS at jku on the card's host (or a jwks URL you name), and ES256, ES384, EdDSA, RS256-512 or PS256-512. Signers prepare the card as served, with empty values removed (a2a-python) or with defaults removed; the answer says which form the signature covers. Verdict signed_verified, signature_failed, unsigned, malformed or not_found.

url.description: a domain, or the card's https URL

card.description: or the card itself, checked offline

jwks.description: a JWKS https URL to read when jku is on another host

algorithms.description: accepted JWS algorithms (default: all asymmetric ones listed)

agents.name: EVM signature check for keys and smart wallets (EIP-191/712, ERC-1271/6492)
agents.description: Did this address sign this? Give signer, signature and the message (EIP-191), the typed data (EIP-712, any types) or the digest. A key's 65-byte or EIP-2098 signature is recovered here with no network. A smart wallet's is asked of the chain in one eth_call of the ERC-6492 universal validator (viem's bytecode), which calls the wallet's isValidSignature (ERC-1271) and, for an ERC-6492 wrapped signature, first runs its factory call so a wallet not deployed yet verifies too. Pinned to one block on Base, Base Sepolia or Ethereum; returns valid, the method, the digest, the EIP-712 domain separator and whether the signer had code (or an EIP-7702 delegate). Changes no state.

signer.description: the address that should have signed

message.description: EIP-191 personal message: text, or 0x hex bytes

block.description: block to check at (default: the latest)

agents.name: RFC 3161 timestamp check: these bytes existed at that time, by that TSA
agents.description: Verifies an RFC 3161 timestamp token or response, offline: the TSTInfo (policy, imprint, serial, genTime, accuracy, nonce), the CMS signed attributes (content type, message digest over the TSTInfo, signingCertificate or V2 naming the signer), the TSA's RSA (PKCS #1 v1.5, PSS) or ECDSA (P-256, P-384) signature, the signer's critical time-stamping key usage, and the chain to a trusted root valid at genTime. Pinned roots: Sigstore's TSA, DigiCert Trusted Root G4 and FreeTSA, matched by public key; add your own as SPKI SHA-256. Give the data, its base64 or its hash to check the imprint. Verdict verified, verified_untrusted, imprint_mismatch or invalid. Not checked: revocation, and whether the TSA's clock was right.

token.description: TimeStampResp or TimeStampToken, DER in base64

trusted_spki.description: extra trusted roots: SHA-256 of their SubjectPublicKeyInfo

agents.name: What a site's robots.txt lets each AI agent do, and what it signals
agents.description: Reads https://<host>/robots.txt and applies RFC 9309 as HISTOR's crawler does: the group naming each product token (else *), the longest matching rule with Allow winning a tie, percent-encoding normalised, * and $; 4xx means everything allowed, 5xx or no answer everything disallowed, same-host redirects followed. Answers, for a path and a list of agents (default: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Google-Extended, PerplexityBot, CCBot, Bytespider, Applebot-Extended, meta-externalagent, Amazonbot, histor and *), allowed or not, the deciding rule and group, and the group's Content-Signal (search, ai-input, ai-train). Also the groups, sitemaps and whether /llms.txt exists. A robots.txt is the site's request, not access control.

url.description: a domain or an https URL

path.description: the path to judge (default: the URL's)

agents.description: product tokens, e.g. GPTBot, ClaudeBot, *

agents.name: x402 preflight: should an agent pay this 402
agents.description: One unpaid request to a paid resource, then everything an agent should know before it signs: the x402 offers (V1 body or V2 PAYMENT-REQUIRED header) with amount in USD, network, asset, payTo, resource and timeout; for the first exact USDC offer on Base or Base Sepolia, whether the asset is that chain's USDC and the EIP-712 domain the token's own (else the signature fails), the amount within your max_usd, payTo valid, the resource on the host called; payTo on chain (key, contract or EIP-7702 delegate) and the USDC it received in the last 24 h, from how many payers; and whether modelmarket.dev lists the seller as an observed x402 seller with its payTo pinned. Verdict looks_payable, review_first, do_not_pay, no_payment_required or not_x402. It pays and signs nothing.

body.description: JSON body for POST, at most 8 KiB

max_usd.description: the most the agent will pay for one call
